author: blueiridium.
content:
I took a look at [consensus-specs #5754](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/5754). The payment inconsistency appears real: with the same slashed proposer and included builder payload, a prompt child leaves the bid canceled, while a child after the pending payment expires reconstructs and charges it.

I don't see a practical attacker motivation to manufacture the late outcome. The proposer gains nothing from self-slashing compared with staying unslashed, and cannot reliably cause the required gap of at least 32 missed mainnet slots. A builder benefits from the prompt-child cancellation, but cannot create genuine slashing evidence against an honest proposer or force that gap. So this seems like a consistency question about the intended payment rule rather than an attacker-driven issue.
